title: Wildlife Tourism in Maharashtra: Tadoba, Pench and Vidarbha's Tiger Country
seoTitle: Wildlife Tourism in Maharashtra: Tadoba & Vidarbha Guide | Kudozz Club
metaDescription: Plan a wildlife trip in Maharashtra: Tadoba, Pench, Umred-Karhandla, Nagzira and Melghat in Vidarbha, plus Bhimashankar, Sanjay Gandhi National Park and birding.
description: A guide to wildlife tourism in Maharashtra: Tadoba Andhari Tiger Reserve and the Vidarbha forests around Nagpur, including Pench, Umred-Karhandla, Nagzira-Navegaon and Melghat, the Sahyadri Tiger Reserve, Bhimashankar's giant squirrels, leopards in Mumbai's Sanjay Gandhi National Park, bird sanctuaries, seasons and routes.
dek: Maharashtra's Vidarbha region, around Nagpur, is some of India's best tiger country. Here is how to plan a wildlife trip across the state.

hero.alt: A tigress and her cubs crossing a lake in Tadoba Andhari Tiger Reserve

intro: Maharashtra had an estimated 444 tigers in the 2022 assessment. Most of them live in Vidarbha, the eastern part of the state around Nagpur and Chandrapur, where Tadoba Andhari Tiger Reserve has become one of India's most popular parks.

The state has six tiger reserves: Tadoba Andhari, Pench, Melghat, Sahyadri, Nagzira-Navegaon and Bor. Closer to Mumbai and Pune, the Western Ghats hold giant squirrels, hornbills and leopards, and Sanjay Gandhi National Park has leopards on the edge of a city of millions.
quickAnswer: Maharashtra's leading wildlife destination is Tadoba Andhari Tiger Reserve near Chandrapur, known for frequent tiger sightings. Other Vidarbha options are Pench (Maharashtra side), Umred-Karhandla, Nagzira-Navegaon and Melghat, all reached from Nagpur. Near Mumbai and Pune, Bhimashankar has Indian giant squirrels and Sanjay Gandhi National Park has leopards. Core zones usually close in the monsoon.
takeaways: Maharashtra had an estimated 444 tigers in 2022, most of them in Vidarbha.
Tadoba is the state's best-known tiger reserve; Nagpur is the gateway.
Tadoba's core zones close in the monsoon; buffer zones can stay open.
Bhimashankar is home to the Indian giant squirrel, the state animal.
Sanjay Gandhi National Park in Mumbai has a resident leopard population.

items.name: The reserve
body: Tadoba National Park and the Andhari Wildlife Sanctuary together form the core, with teak forest, bamboo and lakes. Core gates include Moharli, Kolara and Navegaon, with several buffer gates around them.

image.alt: Forest and water in Tadoba Andhari Tiger Reserve
image.caption: Tadoba Andhari Tiger Reserve

items.name: Wildlife
body: Tigers, leopards, sloth bears, dhole, gaur and marsh crocodiles in Tadoba lake, with a rich bird list.

items.name: Bhimashankar
body: Evergreen forest around the Bhimashankar temple, home to the Indian giant squirrel (shekru).

items.name: Sanjay Gandhi National Park
body: A forest inside Mumbai with leopards, Kanheri caves and a lion and tiger safari enclosure; the wild leopards are rarely seen but live here.

items.name: Sahyadri Tiger Reserve
body: Koyna and Chandoli, remote forest in the Western Ghats, with limited tourism.

sections.heading: Where to stay
list: Tadoba: resorts and lodges near Moharli, Kolara and Navegaon gates, plus forest department stays.
Pench (Maharashtra): lodges near Sillari and Khursapar.
Umred-Karhandla: day trips from Nagpur are easy.
Bhimashankar: simple stays near the temple, or visit from Pune.
Mumbai: Sanjay Gandhi National Park is a half-day trip from anywhere in the city.

sections.heading: How many days to spend
paras: Two or three nights at Tadoba give four to six drives across core and buffer zones. A week from Nagpur covers Tadoba with Pench or Umred-Karhandla. Bhimashankar and Sanjay Gandhi National Park fit into a day each from Pune or Mumbai.

safety: Sightings are never guaranteed; plan several drives and enjoy the forest itself.
Stay in the vehicle on safaris and follow your guide.
Book permits only through official forest department portals or trusted operators.
Never feed animals or leave litter in a park.
Vidarbha summers are extremely hot; carry water and avoid midday outdoors.
packing: Light cotton clothes in neutral colours

faqs.q: Which is the best wildlife sanctuary in Maharashtra?
faqs.a: Tadoba Andhari Tiger Reserve is the most visited for tigers.
Nagpur is the nearest airport, about three hours by road; Chandrapur is the nearest railway station.

faqs.q: How many tiger reserves are in Maharashtra?
faqs.a: Six: Tadoba Andhari, Pench, Melghat, Sahyadri, Nagzira-Navegaon and Bor.
Yes, in Sanjay Gandhi National Park, though they are rarely seen by visitors.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Tadoba?
faqs.a: October to June. March to June is hot but often best for sightings; the core closes in the monsoon.
Tadoba is bigger and known for frequent sightings; Pench is quieter and easy to combine. Many visitors do both.

faqs.q: Where can I see the Indian giant squirrel?
faqs.a: In Bhimashankar Wildlife Sanctuary near Pune.
